item.title: ChatGPT models in Claude Code: gptcc setup and troubleshooting
item.author: william
item.description:
I wanted Claude Code’s terminal interface and tools to run ChatGPT models. Installing gptcc was only the first step. I could select Sol in /model and still get an account-hold error before the request reached GPT.

The working setup uses a local authenticated gateway, ChatGPT OAuth, and Claude Code’s custom model picker. It lists eight GPT models, makes Default resolve to GPT-6.1 Sol with medium effort, and displays Codex’s five-hour and weekly usage beside the model. A real Claude Code session completed a file-read tool call in two turns.

item.title: Installing ChatGPT Desktop on Mint 20 / Ubuntu 20.04 — when the blocker isn't glibc
item.author: william
item.description:
OpenAI shipped an official ChatGPT Desktop for Linux in August 2026 (preview), supporting Ubuntu 24.04/26.04, Debian 13, Fedora 43/44 and Arch. Mint 20.3 (focal, glibc 2.31) is nowhere on that list, so I expected a rerun of the Claude Desktop surgery.

It wasn’t. The glibc floor was fine all along — the package is blocked by three library renames and one optional TPM module. The fix is smaller, and the audit is worth showing because the conclusion is the opposite of last time.
